title: fix: pair gross margin against Pollen revenue, not Stripe cash
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
Gross margin divided Stripe pack cash by all-traffic compute cost — mismatched on both population (most usage is Quest Pollen, no cash) and timing (packs are bought once, burned over later weeks). The row tracked purchase timing, not economics.

- **Gross margin** = (Pollen revenue − compute cost) / Pollen revenue. Same traffic, same week. Reads −1.9% → −17.5% over the last six weeks, degrading steadily; the old row bounced −23% → −222%.
- **Cash coverage** is the old ratio, correctly named: Stripe pack revenue ÷ the week's compute cost.

Both read fields the live pipe already returns — **no Tinybird change**.

Not modelled, on purpose: vendor credits (would need a pipe change plus a hand-maintained list of live grants, and a wrong list reads as confident profit), salaries (engineering is R&D, not cost of delivery), Stripe fees.

gist.headline: The ledger gets pollenated
gist.blurb: The KPI garden got two correctly labeled measuring sticks. One follows Pollen as it is used; the other keeps an eye on pack purchases.
gist.summary: Updated the KPI dashboard to calculate gross margin from same-week Pollen revenue and compute cost, while preserving the previous Stripe-pack-cash-to-compute-cost ratio as separately named cash coverage.
gist.impact: Internal operators can now distinguish usage-aligned gross margin from purchase-timing cash coverage without changing the live Tinybird data pipeline.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy garden accounting scene: Polli compares two clearly separate glowing pixel ledger columns, one marked Pollen and compute sprouts and the other marked pack coins and a calendar, showing that two useful measurements should not be mixed. A small CRT monitor robot helps hold the reports amid code-plants and flowers.
